title: FIG Log Entry
description: One line of the log = one JSON object matching this schema. Two entry types share an envelope: 'seam' (a linkage that broke, noticed in a retro/postmortem/PR/or in the moment) and 'faces' (a per-cycle FACES score). See log-template.md for field-by-field notes and worked examples.

domain.description: One of the 21 domains of integration from ../domains-of-integration.md, or 'other' if none fit. Slugs are lowercase_with_underscores versions of the doc's domain names.

antiPattern.description: One of the 8 named anti-patterns from ../anti-patterns.md, or 'other'. Optional — a seam can break without matching a named anti-pattern.

id.description: ULID (sortable by creation time, no coordination needed). Any unique, time-sortable ID works if you'd rather generate it another way.

system.description: Open vocabulary, not a strict enum — yours to grow. A reasonable starting set: one entry per project or area of life you apply FIG to. Keep it short and consistent so you can filter/group by it later.

source_other.description: Required when source is 'other'. Free text.

notes.description: Free text. Always optional, always welcome.

domain_other.description: Required when domain is 'other'. If this keeps happening for the same kind of seam, it's a signal a 22nd domain wants naming — that's principle 2 (deliberate differentiation), applied to this schema.

seam.description: Name the boundary, not the component — e.g. 'mobile client <-> API token refresh', not 'the API'.

what_broke.description: What actually happened at that boundary.

action.description: What closes the loop. Can be filled in later, when status moves to closed.

owner.description: Who's responsible for the action. Matters once this spans more than one person.

landed.description: How far the fix has propagated past the branch it was made on. Orthogonal to `status`: a seam can be `status: closed` (the fix is done and verified) while still `landed: branch` (not yet merged to the trunk, let alone deployed). `branch`: fixed and verified in isolation. `merged`: merged into the trunk/main line. `live`: merged and confirmed running where real usage happens. Optional — omit for systems with no such distinction (trunk-based dev, no separate deploy step).

landed_date.description: Set when `landed` last changed — e.g. the day a branch-verified fix actually reached main.

cycle.description: An identifier for the cycle this score covers, e.g. '2026-W37' or 'sprint 24'. Reuse the same convention per system so consecutive cycles sort/compare cleanly.

integration_move.description: The one committed action for next cycle (retrospective.md's 'one integration move'). Can be filled in after scores if you fill this out live.

move_status.description: Lets the next cycle's loop-check be a query instead of a recollection: 'find last faces entry for this system, check move_status'.
